title: Exam preparation: self-directed revision of the unit before the summative assessment

learning_objectives.text: describe data and computer systems protection measures such as: physical risks, inter-network screens, information encryption, biometrics, computer virus
use data protection measures such as data backup and disk mirroring
analyse ethical problems arising due to computer system cracking
analyse problems arising due to malware
analyse problems arising due to disseminating and using information

lesson_objectives.all: find the topics of the unit where they are missing points, revise them and complete the missing practice, notes or Exam Mode
lesson_objectives.most: reach the points needed before the summative assessment (2 for practice, 2 for notes and 2 for Exam Mode in each lesson) and correct their mistakes using the feedback
lesson_objectives.some: explain the hardest ideas of the unit to a classmate and answer longer exam-style questions (analyse, explain, evaluate) at full marks

assessment_criteria.criterion: Identify and close their own learning gaps in the unit
descriptors: reads the Points page and names the lessons with missing points
sets a realistic target for the lesson and plans the order of work
completes the missing practice, notes and Exam Mode and checks the result

assessment_criteria.criterion: Apply the knowledge of the unit in exam-style questions
descriptors: describes protection measures and backup methods with correct terms
analyses problems caused by cracking, malware and disseminating information
names copyright protection rules, explains anti-plagiarism checks and E-gov services

learners_can: describe their progress and plan (I still need …, first I will …)
explain a term to a classmate in their own words
answer command words correctly (describe, explain, analyse)
phrases: I am missing points in … because …
This answer gets full marks because it …

values.action: Learners revise in their own notebooks and answer Exam Mode on their own; copied notes or answers earn no points.
Learners take responsibility for their own revision: they find their gaps, set a target and check their progress.
In the peer-help block learners who have finished a topic explain it to classmates who still need it.

cross_curricular: Law: computer crime, personal data and copyright in the Republic of Kazakhstan.
English: command words, definitions and extended answers.
Self-management: planning and tracking one's own learning.
ict: ICT Practice Platform: Points page (missing points per lesson), theory, practice with automatic feedback, notes upload and Exam Mode.
Teacher → Points: the teacher sees every learner's points live and calls those who are behind.
Learners' own laptops; notebooks photographed and uploaded for checking.
previous_learning: All lessons of unit 12.2A: methods of information systems protection, data protection measures, intellectual property protection, E-gov resources and checking documents for plagiarism.

blocks.title: Greeting and lesson goal
blocks.teacher: Explains that the summative assessment is next lesson and that today every learner revises on their own and collects the points still missing. Shows the rules: best attempt counts, notes are full at 70%, Exam Mode is full at 80%.
blocks.learners: Listen and ask questions about the summative assessment and the points.
resources: Slide: lesson goal, the points rules and the summative date

blocks.title: Self-check: my points and my target
blocks.teacher: Asks learners to open the Points page; on Teacher → Points marks the learners with the most missing points to visit first.
blocks.learners: Open the Points page, list the lessons of the unit with missing practice, notes or Exam Mode and write a target and a plan in their notebook (for example: 1) Data protection L3 notes, 2) Malware practice, 3) Exam Mode of Intellectual property).

poll.question: Which topic of the unit do you feel least ready for?

blocks.title: Revision block 1: close the biggest gap
blocks.teacher: Moves around the class starting with the learners who are furthest behind; helps them choose the right theory section and checks they read feedback instead of guessing. Answers questions one to one.
blocks.learners: Work through the plan: read the theory of the weakest topic, write or finish handwritten notes and upload a photo, do the practice questions until the practice points are full, read the feedback on wrong answers.

blocks.title: Mini-review: common mistakes
blocks.teacher: Shows 3 typical mistakes from today's practice (for example: backup vs disk mirroring, virus vs worm, copyright vs patent) and how a full-mark answer looks for the command words describe, explain and analyse.
blocks.learners: Compare with their own answers and correct their notes.
resources: Slide: 3 common mistakes and model answers

blocks.title: Revision block 2: Exam Mode
blocks.teacher: Reminds learners to sit Exam Mode only after the practice and notes of that lesson; watches progress on Teacher → Points and keeps the room quiet for exam conditions.
blocks.learners: Sit Exam Mode for the lessons where the exam points are missing or below 80%, on their own and without notes; learners who already have full points do longer exam-style questions from the practice.

blocks.title: Peer help
blocks.teacher: Pairs learners who have finished a topic with learners who still need it (random pairs on the host's laptop, swapped if both need the same help).
blocks.learners: The helper explains the topic in their own words and asks two quick questions; the partner continues their plan. Helpers do not give answers to Exam Mode.
resources: Random pairs on the host's laptop

blocks.title: Progress check
blocks.teacher: Checks Teacher → Points and names what is still missing for each group of learners; reminds them of the deadline before the summative assessment.
blocks.learners: Open the Points page again, tick the targets they reached and write what is left for homework.

blocks.title: Reflection and homework
blocks.teacher: Asks the reflection question and sets homework: finish all missing points of the unit before the summative assessment.
blocks.learners: Answer the poll and say one thing they still need to revise.

poll.question: How ready are you for the summative assessment now?
options: I need more time on several topics

safety: Laptops on the desk, charging cables kept off the walkways.
Short screen breaks: look away from the screen during the mini-review.

support: The teacher visits learners with the most missing points first and helps them build a short plan.
Notes checklists show exactly what a full-mark notebook contains.
Learners who struggle start with practice (instant feedback) before Exam Mode; peer helpers explain hard topics.
stretch: Learners with full points answer longer analyse/evaluate questions and act as peer helpers.
They compare two protection measures or two licences in a written answer with a justified conclusion.

assessment: Self-assessment: targets in the notebook, ticked at the end of the lesson.
Automatic feedback in practice; notes checked against the checklist; Exam Mode marked by the mark scheme.
The teacher tracks every learner live on Teacher → Points and gives oral feedback one to one.
Polls at the start and the end show how confident learners feel.
reflection: Did every learner know which points they were missing and have a plan?
Which topics were most often weak, and what should be repeated before the summative assessment?
Who still needs support after this lesson?
